The fault is localized to the shared interval-location semantics, not the polynomial formula itself. Out-of-range inputs are mapped to a boundary table row while the value and gradient kernels then interpret that mapping differently from the original input; the upper end is especially severe because it evaluates the start of the last interval instead of its endpoint. I’m checking the tensor/attention variants and the adjoint kernels now, since they must all use one identical extension rule.

Implemented the compressed-tabulation repair in [tabulate.cc](/workspace/task/source/lib/src/tabulate.cc:26).

The root cause was inconsistent out-of-support handling: forward kernels clipped inputs to a table row while gradient kernels still returned a nonzero polynomial derivative. At the upper limit, the last interval was also evaluated at its start instead of its endpoint.

The repair now:

- Continues values beyond table support using the endpoint tangent:

- Uses the same endpoint derivative in forward, gradient, and gradient-gradient kernels.
- Applies consistently to `se_a`, attention-enabled `se_a`, `se_r`, `se_t`, and `se_t_tebd`.
- Computes interval counts with rounded arithmetic and bounds interval indices, avoiding floating-point truncation errors for valid stride layouts.
- Supports both float and double instantiations.
